events.title: Demo 1.7.4: a hand that shows you how
events.summary: Thank you to everyone trying the demo during Steam Next Fest. Your sessions showed me where people get stuck at the start: many left the first mission without placing a single part. This update is for them. events.title: La Bidouillerie at Steam Next Fest
events.summary: Steam Next Fest runs from October 19 to 26, starting at 10 AM Pacific time. La Bidouillerie is taking part with its free demo.A real electronics simulator: build a machine from an electromechanical kit, snap solenoids and gears onto a perforated chassis, wire the circuit, switch on. It moves, sparks or burns. Twelve missions, a 1970s pinball table, a sandbox; the dart machine and transistors come in the full game.You can download the demo from the game's store page. events.title: La Bidouillerie 1.7 — Eight languages
events.summary: Eight languages La Bidouillerie now speaks French, English, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, Simplified Chinese, German and Japanese. Every line of the game and every one of the eighty-nine Encyclopedia pages, in each of them. Eight flags on the players screen, and a Windows set to one of these languages starts the game in it — which it did not until now: every newcomer started in French whatever their system. events.title: La Bidouillerie 1.6 — Build a pinball machine
events.summary: A second bench: the pinball machine After the twelve vacuum-robot missions, the workshop opens a pinball cabinet — the drilled playfield, the backbox, and the same kit of parts to screw onto them. You trace your walls, you wire your flippers, you arm the transformer, and you shoot the ball. Five new missions, and the table stays playable at every step. events.title: A mistake I'm keeping
events.summary: I hadn't planned to show the pinball table yet. It's still on the bench, it isn't finished, and it was meant to stay behind a closed door. Except the door wasn't closed: the workshop unlocked as early as the fourth vacuum mission, and all it took was a trip back through the Players menu to walk straight into it. Several of you found it. So much for the surprise — and just as well, because it made up my mind to build it properly. {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/46268659/a39a7a44feab62f4f28eab555f9a2f0e8d52a9a

events.title: Right-click now opens a part's data sheet
events.summary: Left-click meant two things at once. Brief, it opened a part's data sheet; held down, it grabbed that part to move it. Two gestures on one button, and nothing to tell you which one was expected.Several players left during the very first mission without ever finding how to push a solenoid's plunger. If that was you, it wasn't you.From now on, a brief right-click on a part opens its sheet. A right-click on empty space closes it, and a cross has appeared in the sheet's corner. events.title: The demo is out
events.summary: The La Bidouillerie demo is out. You can download it from this page, free.A perforated chassis, a crate of parts, and a robot that has to roll. The mechanics bolt underneath, the wiring goes on top. You switch the power on, and that is when you find out what you missed.Nothing is faked. The current is genuinely computed, ten thousand times a second. Your machine stalls at dead centre until you fit a flywheel.
